Hi Sam —

Thanks again for the call last week. Attached is our updated renewal proposal (v2) and a conservative usage forecast for the next 12 months. Key options we included for Neptune: 

- 12-month term with a phased commit (Q1 conservative baseline + ability to uplift each quarter)
- Conditional surge buffer: temporary burst allowance that avoids overage shocks during peak seasonal windows
- Ramp credit: one-time credit applied to invoice if Neptune increases commit by >=20% at signing

What I'd like to highlight: we can offer a time-bound price hold on the committed tier for the first 3 months of the new term if Neptune agrees to the commit uplift and an executive-level review in Q2. That gives you breathing room during the holiday peak while protecting your unit economics.

I've attached: neptune_renewal_proposal_v2.pdf (terms + pricing ladder) and usage_forecast_q1-q4.xlsx.

Hi Lauren —

Thanks for the proposal — appreciated the rapid turnaround. A few follow-ups from our side: 

1) For the holiday surge window (Nov–Jan) we need assurance we won't face punitive overage rates. Is the temporary burst allowance guaranteed, or is it subject to manual approval each time?
2) Procurement is asking for a partial price hold on the per-token rate for committed usage for at least the first quarter — we need predictability while the new features are ramping.
3) We'd prefer credits to be invoiced/visible up front rather than as a post-facto invoice credit, procurement wants to see impact to TCO in the contract.

From a commercial perspective, we're comfortable considering an uplift to commit, but timeline matters: we need a signed amendment by Dec 1 to get budget approval for the holiday inventory. Can Redwood provide a clean redline and confirm the effective date alignment?

If you can send a revised term sheet showing (a) a guaranteed burst buffer with defined thresholds, (b) a first-quarter price hold, and (c) an upfront ramp credit applied to the initial invoice, we can accelerate.

Thanks —
Sam

Marissa / Ben — forwarding Sam's request. Quick summary and suggested trade: 

- Customer asks: guaranteed burst buffer for Nov–Jan, first-quarter price hold on committed tier, and upfront credits visible on invoice.
- Our possible trade: require a 20% uplift to committed baseline (annualized) in exchange for:
  * a 10% concession off committed unit price for Q1 only (applied to committed units),
  * a one-time $50,000 ramp credit applied to the initial invoice (shows on invoice as line item),
  * explicit burst buffer definition: +30% monthly usage above committed baseline for three months before overage rates kick in.

Operational notes: if we grant the buffer and Q1 hold, we should include a hard review at the end of Q1 with Ops to validate usage and adjust kernels/pinning to keep latency SLOs. Also recommend adding an automatic fallback to a compatible model variant if peak latency exceeds SLA — helps protect us from unbounded ops cost.

Risks: Finance will want to ensure $50k credit doesn't cascade into larger concessions if the customer later reduces commit. Suggest credit clawback clause if they downscale below original baseline within 90 days.

Can you confirm approval for the $50k credit and Q1 concession? If yes, I'll draft a clean redline and loop in legal.

Thanks,
Lauren

Hi Sam —

Thanks — we can accommodate the asks with the following conditioned package: 

1) Term & Commit: 12-month term effective Dec 1, 2026. Neptune will increase the annual committed usage baseline by 20% at signing (documented in schedule A).

2) Q1 Price Hold: Redwood will hold the committed-tier unit price for committed usage for Jan 1–Mar 31, 2027. This applies only to the committed units (not burst usage).

3) Burst Buffer: Guaranteed buffer of +30% monthly usage above committed baseline for the three-month seasonal window (Dec–Feb). Overage rates apply only above that threshold. Buffer is predefined and does not require ad hoc approvals once signed.

4) Ramp Credit: One-time $50,000 credit applied as a line item on the initial invoice (clearly visible to procurement). Credit carries a clawback if Neptune reduces annual committed usage below the pre-signing baseline within 90 days of the term start.

5) Operational Safeguards: We will include an Ops review 60 days post-go-live. If latency regressions occur during the buffer window, Redwood will automatically shift requests to a lower-cost compatible variant to preserve SLOs and limit ops spend; we'll notify Neptune before any extended fallback.

Attached is a clean redline (redline-term-sheet-v3.docx) and a short summary PDF. Please review and let me know if procurement needs any tweaks — if this matches what you need, we can route to Legal for a fast-track amendment and target signature by Nov 30.

Appreciate the partnership — looking forward to locking this in.

Best,
